TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyPlayer in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

Applied by generate_random_potion_in_combat (potion_pools.py:138-145) and NOT by generate_random_potion, matching PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionInCombat vs ...OutOfCombat (PotionFactory.cs:31-34, 60-65).

OnUse (protected override, FruitJuice.cs.rationale: `CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(target, MaxHp.BaseValue)` -> `CreatureCmd.gain_max_hp(hooks, player, 5)`, which raises max_hp and then heals the same amount (cmds.py:175-176) -- the SetMaxHp-then-Heal shape the sim's own docstring cites. The amount is an integer literal on both sides so the decimal truncation that blood_potion N1 settles cannot arise here.

guards.what: N1: this is the one potion whose effect PERSISTS past the combat, so the in-combat/out-of-combat split is not cosmetic
guards.rationale: Max HP is run state, and the sim keeps a separate run-side twin for it (RunState.gain_max_hp, named at cmds.py:172). The combat-side verb this potion uses writes PlayerCombatState.max_hp, and RunState.finish_combat is what carries it back to the run -- the same route every in-combat max-HP change takes, so nothing is specific to this potion. Recorded because it is the reachability half of this record's AnyTime gap: a Fruit Juice drunk on the map in a recorded run changes the max HP the conformance runner asserts at the next act boundary (conformance/runner.py's DETECTOR 3 player-HP assertion), so that gap is not merely theoretical.
